answer: A verifiable delay function protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to compute sequential, non-parallelizable cryptographic proofs before registering. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating physical processor cores over elapsed wall-clock time per identity. Whether an agent maps an opal cache near a mesa or monitors an active ember, it cannot bypass these serial compute cycles. However, this mandatory delay increases latency and penalizes energy-constrained nodes.
